name: Floor and Mod
description: A pair of positive integers $$$(a,b)$$$ is called special if $$$\lfloor \frac{a}{b} \rfloor = a \bmod b$$$. Here, $$$\lfloor \frac{a}{b} \rfloor$$$ is the result of the integer division between $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, while $$$a \bmod b$$$ is its remainder. You are given two integers $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$. Find the number of special pairs $$$(a,b)$$$ such that $$$1\leq a \leq x$$$ and $$$1 \leq b \leq y$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 100$$$) — the number of test cases. The only line of the description of each test case contains two integers $$$x$$$, $$$y$$$ ($$$1 \le x,y \le 10^9$$$).
output_specification: For each test case print the answer on a single line.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1485C — Floor and Mod [242. Sieve, Prime Factorization and Divisors]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Every composite integer $X$ has at least one prime factor $\le \sqrt{X}$. Precomputing the Smallest Prime Factor (SPF) for all numbers up to $M$ via a linear sieve allows any $X \le M$ to be completely prime-factorized in $O(\log X)$ steps.
